s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive scalp mass with ulceration and bleeding, associated with cervical lymphadenopathy and suspected distant metastases
salient_findings: Ulceration and easy bleeding of the mass
key_facts: 10-year history of right-sided scalp mass
Mass was stable and nontender until excision 5 months ago
Mass recurred, enlarged, ulcerated, and bled easily after excision
Patient denied headaches, convulsions, or neurologic deficits
Patient was afebrile and hemodynamically stable
No pallor, jaundice, or palpable peripheral lymphadenopathy
Two lesions on the right side of the scalp
Laboratory studies showed normal complete blood count and basic metabolic panel
Chest radiography and abdominal/pelvic ultrasound were unremarkable
Head and neck CT scan showed multilobulated, hyperdense, ulcerative right frontal scalp lesion
MRI of the spine revealed pathological compression fracture of T10 and hyperintense lesion in T8
